svg.title: Sheet 1 of 2 - Battery system
svg.desc: A 5 V source feeds the CN3303 boost charger, which charges a 3S Li-ion pack through a BMS. The pack goes through a fuse and master switch to the motor driver, the NPK sensor, a 5 V buck converter and a resistor divider that lets the Arduino measure battery percentage.
svg.text: Rover electronics · Sheet 1 of 2 · rev A · 2026-10-03
Charge (CN3303) → protect (3S BMS) → fuse & switch → distribute → measure battery %

svg.text: Typical 18650 cells at rest, ±10 %. Calibrate against a multimeter,
and keep the buck at 5.00 V because it is also the ADC reference.
6.7 kΩ source: fine for the ADC
1. The CN3303 is a BOOST charger: its input is 3–6 V. Feed it 5 V at ≥ 2 A; anything above 6 V can destroy it.
2. It neither balances nor protects the cells. The 3S BMS must sit between the pack, the charger and every load.
3. Charge with SW1 OFF: a running load starves the charger and it cannot see end-of-charge.
4. Keep F1 close to the pack so a short downstream cannot start a fire; use wire rated for the current (≥ 0.5 mm²).
5. Upload code over USB with SW1 OFF, and never power the 5V pin and USB at the same time.
6. Battery % is valid only with the motors idle and the charger unplugged: the pack sags under load and rises on charge.
7. Wire polarity first, power second: a reversed pack destroys the buck, the L298N and the Arduino.
Bring-up checks with a multimeter (before the Arduino is plugged in)
a. SW1 OFF, 5 V into the charger: CR LED lights and B+ to GND climbs toward 12.6 V as the pack fills.
b. SW1 ON: VBAT_SW to GND equals the pack voltage (9.6–12.6 V).
c. Buck OUT+ to GND: trim to 5.00 V before wiring any 5 V load.
d. Divider mid-point to GND: VBAT ÷ 3 (about 3.70 V at 11.1 V).
